newsitem.title: USA: Gang member confesses to Olympic guardsman's murder.
newsitem.headline: Gang member confesses to Olympic guardsman's murder.

text.p: A 19-year-old reputed gang member has confessed to the murder of an off-duty National Guardsman who was slain two months ago while on assignment with the Olympic security force, police said on Wednesday.

Spc. Juventino Silva, a 25-year-old member of the Indiana National Guard, was gunned down early on Aug. 4 as he and a fellow guardsman walked back to their billet in this Atlanta suburb from a nearby nightclub. His companion, Sgt. Danny Cook, 43, was grazed by a single bullet during the attack.

Both men were part of a 400-member contingent from the Indiana Guard that was in Atlanta to provide security for the Centennial Olympic Games. They had been scheduled to return home the day after the shooting.
Police were puzzled by the murder until Monday, when state crime lab results showed that the same .25-calibre handgun had been used in a recent gang-initiation killing.

The suspect, John Eccles, and a 20-year-old man, both described by police as members of the Crips gang, were already in custody for the latest incident, in which a woman was shot to death and her sister was stabbed.
"We confronted Mr. Eccles and he confessed to the (Silva) murder," Doraville Police Maj. Clifford Edwards said in an interview aired on Atlanta NBC-affiliate WXIA-TV.
"Both murders were within a mile of each other. Both murders were violent -- a lot of shots fired into the victims. And we knew what weapon was used."
